title: Retry policy maintenance with edge cases
final_response:
Done. `retry_policy.py` now implements the documented contract:

```python
def should_retry(method,status,attempt):
    """Retry GET/HEAD only, on 429 or 503, and only while attempt < 3. attempt starts at 1."""
    return str(method).upper() in ("GET", "HEAD") and status in (429, 503) and attempt < 3
```

- **Method:** only `GET`/`HEAD`, case-insensitive via `str(...).upper()`
- **Status:** exactly `429` or `503` (no blanket `>= 500`)
- **Attempt:** `< 3` (i.e., attempts 1 and 2 retry; 3 and beyond don't)

Verification: `python3 test_visible.py` → "visible tests PASS". Additionally, 28 edge-case checks pass covering mixed-case methods (`head`, `GeT`), other methods (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `OPTIONS`, empty string), neighboring statuses (`500`, `502`, `504`, `400`, `418`, `200`), and the attempt boundary (1, 2 → retry; 3, 999 → no). Attempt values outside the documented domain (docstring says attempts start at 1) are not special-cased — the rule is applied literally as `attempt < 3`.
